desc: Read the integer N and strings S and T from standard input.

Check for feasibility: Iterate through all indices i from 0 to N-1; if S[i] != T[i], verify that for all other indices j where S[j] == S[i], T[j] must also equal T[i]. If any mismatch is found where S[i] == S[j] but T[i] != T[j], output -1 immediately.
Identify the set of characters in S that need to be changed (those where S[i] != T[i]).

Determine the minimum operations by counting the number of unique characters in S that appear in positions where S[i] != T[i]. Since each operation replaces a specific character globally, the minimum number of operations is simply the count of unique characters in S that are not already matching T at their respective positions (provided the feasibility check passed).
Print the calculated minimum number of operations.

Implement the solution: Read N, S, T. Check consistency: For each char `c` in 'a'-'z', if it appears in S, it must map to a unique char in T. If `S[i] == S[j]` but `T[i] != T[j]`, print -1. Build the dependency graph (adjacency list or map). Detect cycles in the graph. Since each node has out-degree <= 1, we can use a visited array and recursion/iteration to detect cycles. If a cycle is found (and it's not a self-loop), print -1. Count the number of edges `u -> v` where `u != v`. Print the count.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
